Lessons.Title: Building Quadratic Functions to Describe Situations (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: build a projectile-height quadratic from an initial height and upward velocity minus a gravitational term, read zeros and vertex of the resulting graph, and restrict real-world time to the flight. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U06:L06 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/6/6/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/6/6/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source contrasts a linear no-gravity launch with a curved gravity-adjusted trajectory.

Original hypothetical model for a soft ball launched vertically: initial height2m, upward velocity12m/s, and an invented approximate gravity term −2t²m. Height h(t)=2+12t−2t² for t≥0 until impact. Without gravity the linear model would be2+12t, which keeps growing; the quadratic bends downward and gives an eventual maximum.

Complete the square: h(t)=20−2(t−3)². Maximum height20m occurs at t3 seconds. Solve h(t)=0: t²−6t−1=0, roots t=3±√10; only positive time t≈6.1623s is physically relevant. A model of height below ground beyond that input is not a real flight prediction.

Student task: graph the original points at t0,1,2,3,4,5 and approximate impact time; compare the no-gravity line and curved height; explain why a root can be algebraically correct but physically inadmissible. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for physical quantity definitions, vertex/zero mathematics, graph/domain and critique of the linear assumption.

KeyConcepts.Title: Projectile height model
KeyConcepts.Definition: Initial height plus upward linear motion minus downward quadratic acceleration.

KeyConcepts.Title: Vertex
KeyConcepts.Definition: A downward-opening quadratic has a maximum at its vertex.

KeyConcepts.Title: Zeros and flight domain
KeyConcepts.Definition: The ground-level root marks the end of the modeled flight.

Steps: Negative root3−√10≈−0.162 is not elapsed flight time.
Positive root3+√10≈6.162s is model impact time.
WorkedExamples.Check: The physical domain ends at ground impact.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating a gravity-free line as realistic forever
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: An upward object slows and falls under gravity.

SummaryPoints: Quadratic launch models combine initial height, linear launch velocity and downward curvature.
The original parabola peaks at t3 with height20m.
The physical ground time is 3+√10 seconds.
Teacher reviews graph, units and real-world limitations.
